overall_summary: Bitcoin is under clear pressure as it tests the 200-week moving average near sixty-eight thousand, with heavy ETF outflows and large liquidations adding to the weight. Hot CPI, rising odds of a December hike, five-percent yields, and a strong dollar keep the macro backdrop hostile for risk assets. A few institutional bids and cooler PPI offer little relief against the broader risk-off tone from rates and geopolitics.
key_points: BTC testing critical 200-week MA support near $68K
ETF outflows and liquidations signal weak demand
Hot CPI and 5% yields keep Fed hike odds elevated
Strong DXY and geo oil risks add risk-off pressure
JPMorgan IBIT add is rare institutional bright spot

items.title: Bitcoin Crashes Below $69K Amid $1.5B Liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin plunged roughly 7 percent over 24 hours to near 68,000 dollars, its lowest since August, as Nvidia CEO resignation turmoil hit risk assets alongside stronger dollar and Fed hike bets. Crypto liquidations hit 1.4 to 1.6 billion dollars, overwhelmingly longs. Traders should watch closely because forced selling cascades can accelerate moves lower if key supports fail.
items.impact: Amplified downside pressure and volatility from leverage flush

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Bleed $1.44B in Five-Day Outflow Streak
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded five consecutive days of net outflows totaling about 1.44 billion dollars through November 11, led heavily by BlackRock IBIT, flipping year-to-date flows deeply negative. Net assets sit near 94 billion dollars. This dries up a major institutional bid and helps explain the spot price weakness traders are navigating.
items.impact: Sustained lack of institutional buying demand

items.title: Bitcoin Tests Critical 200-Week Moving Average Near $68K
items.summary: Bitcoin briefly tagged or slipped under its 200-week simple moving average around 68,000 dollars for the first time in about 11 weeks. This long-term average has historically marked major cycle lows and support zones. A confirmed hold and bounce would be constructive for bulls while a clean break could open deeper correction targets, making it the key technical level right now.
items.impact: Unresolved long-term support test that could decide next major leg

items.title: MSCI Removes Strategy and Metaplanet From Indexes Nov 30
items.summary: MSCI confirmed it will delete Bitcoin treasury company Strategy from its USA, World and ACWI indexes and Metaplanet from the Japan Small Cap Index effective the November 30 close under new non-operating company rules. Passive funds tracking those benchmarks will sell the shares. This reduces a source of capital for further Bitcoin purchases by the largest public holders.
items.impact: Forced share selling and tighter funding for BTC treasury firms

items.title: Nakamoto Owes Kraken $165M, Exceeding Full Market Cap
items.summary: Bitcoin treasury firm Nakamoto amended its 165 million USDT loan with Kraken to push remaining principal into 2027 after the company's market value fell below the debt load. Roughly 70 percent of its Bitcoin is pledged as collateral, now covering the loan more thinly after the price drop. Further declines raise margin-call or forced-sale risks that could add spot supply.
items.impact: Elevated forced-selling risk from leveraged Bitcoin holder

items.title: JPMorgan Boosts Strategy Stake 36 Percent, Holds $540M IBIT
items.summary: JPMorgan's latest 13F filing shows it raised its Strategy common shares 36 percent in the third quarter to about 849,000 shares and increased BlackRock IBIT holdings 9.6 percent to 11.4 million shares worth roughly 540 million dollars as of September 30. The bank also holds other crypto-linked names. This demonstrates continued large-bank exposure even through the recent selloff.
items.impact: Reinforces institutional allocation narrative despite near-term weakness

items.title: October PPI cools: MoM falls 0.1%, YoY slows to 2.3%
items.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported producer prices eased in October, with the final demand PPI down 0.1 percent on the month and up just 2.3 percent year-over-year, decelerating from 2.7 percent. Goods prices dropped 0.2 percent, led by energy, while core measures held steadier around 2.6 percent. For traders this softens upstream inflation pressure after the hot CPI, potentially dialing back the most aggressive December hike bets even as services stay sticky.
items.impact: Could temper extreme hawkish pricing and support risk assets if confirmed as trend

items.title: US 10-year yield tops 5%, DXY hits 19-month high
items.summary: Treasury yields climbed sharply with the 10-year pushing above 5.1 percent and the two-year surging in its biggest multi-day move in years. The dollar index held near 103.2, its strongest since April 2025 and on track for the best week in two months. Crypto traders should watch this closely because higher real rates and a strong dollar historically pressure Bitcoin and risk assets by raising the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets.
items.impact: Tighter financial conditions and stronger USD headwinds for crypto and equities

items.title: NY Fed's Williams: inflation far too high, more work needed
items.summary: New York Fed President John Williams said Thursday evening that inflation remains stubbornly elevated and the central bank still has work to do to get policy to the right place. He called the economy strong with a firming labor market, signaling more rate increases are likely over time to return inflation to 2 percent. This keeps the December hike firmly in play and reinforces the higher-for-longer narrative that weighs on liquidity-sensitive markets like crypto.
items.impact: Solidifies market pricing for further Fed tightening into year-end

items.title: Hot October CPI keeps December hike odds near certain
items.summary: Tuesday's CPI print of plus 0.4 percent headline and 0.3 percent core, both above forecasts, continues to dominate pricing. Markets now assign roughly 85 to 91 percent odds to a 25 basis point hike in December, with some officials floating a possible 50 basis point move if pressures persist. For Bitcoin traders this means elevated rate volatility and a less friendly liquidity backdrop heading into the FOMC.
items.impact: Entrenches hawkish Fed path and higher discount rates for risk assets

items.title: Existing home sales sink to 16-year low in October
items.summary: Existing home sales dropped 5.5 percent to a 3.75 million annualized pace, the slowest since August 2010, missing forecasts as higher mortgage rates sidelined buyers. Inventory rose and months of supply hit multi-year highs while median prices edged up slightly. This housing weakness signals the lagged impact of tighter policy and could eventually feed into slower growth or Fed caution, though it is secondary to inflation data right now.
items.impact: Highlights rate sensitivity in housing; mixed signal for growth vs inflation

items.title: Initial jobless claims rise to 200,000, topping estimates
items.summary: Weekly initial claims climbed to 200,000 for the week ending November 7, above the roughly 195,000 consensus and up from a revised 191,000. Continuing claims eased slightly. The labor market remains solid overall but this modest uptick adds a small soft data point amid otherwise firm employment readings and keeps the dual-mandate debate alive for the Fed.
items.impact: Mild cooling signal that may slightly offset pure hawkishness

items.title: Trump Says No Iran Deal Needed, Sidelines Vance
items.summary: President Trump declared the US no longer needs a deal with Iran and ordered Vice President Vance to drop negotiations and focus on alleged corruption in Democratic cities instead. This came after midterm losses partly blamed on the war and as backchannel talks were advancing. Oil prices jumped on the news as traders priced in prolonged Middle East supply risks and a naval blockade remaining in place. Crypto traders should watch because higher oil feeds inflation fears and rate hike bets that pressure risk assets including Bitcoin.
items.impact: Higher oil and energy risk premium weighs on risk assets and crypto

items.title: Iran Claims Strike on US Radar in Bahrain
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted and destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in retaliation for an alleged US strike on telecom infrastructure in southern Iran. It is the first such claim against American military assets in a Gulf country since early September amid the fragile lull in the wider conflict. No immediate US or Bahrain confirmation, but it raises fresh escalation risks around the Strait of Hormuz. Traders care because any Gulf military flare-up threatens oil flows and can spike volatility across energy and risk markets.
items.impact: Escalation risk lifts oil and risk-off pressure on crypto

items.title: Europe to Join Next Ukraine Peace Talks
items.summary: After US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Putin in Moscow, Russia agreed to let European representatives join the next round of peace talks with Ukraine. Zelensky confirmed Europe will have a voice, following Abu Dhabi talks that produced a major prisoner exchange but no territorial breakthrough. Putin remains hardline on territory and rejects foreign troops. This is key for markets as any credible path to ending the nearly five-year war could ease European energy and security risk premiums that have weighed on global risk appetite.
items.impact: De-escalation hopes support risk assets if talks advance

items.title: UK Sanctions All Top 10 Russian Oil Producers
items.summary: Britain became the first country to sanction all ten of Russia's largest oil producers, adding Slavneft plus shadow fleet vessels, coal companies and Rosneft's Vostok Oil project. The package was announced as European leaders met in Dublin focused on Ukraine support and peace efforts. It aims to further squeeze Moscow's war funding. Energy traders and crypto desks should note potential further pressure on Russian supply chains and any knock-on effects to global oil pricing or European gas dynamics.
items.impact: Tightens Russia energy revenues; limited near-term oil spike risk

items.title: Israeli Strike Hits Gaza Nasser Hospital
items.summary: An Israeli airstrike on Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis killed at least six people including a surgeon, the deadliest single incident since recent elections, according to Gaza health officials. Israel said it targeted a Hamas brigade commander and militants using the site as a headquarters; Hamas denied the claim and called it a war crime. The strike damaged surgical and ICU facilities serving a large population. While primarily a humanitarian and regional story, continued Gaza violence keeps Middle East risk elevated alongside the Iran conflict.
items.impact: Sustains regional tension without major new oil shock

items.title: Oil Rebounds on Iran Stalemate and Hormuz Risks
items.summary: Brent crude jumped over three percent after Trump's no-deal comments and held near ninety-six dollars as Iran claimed the Bahrain radar strike and tanker incidents continued in the Strait of Hormuz. Shipping attacks and infrastructure threats keep a geopolitical premium in the market even as some Middle East flows recover. Higher oil reinforces inflation concerns and supports bets on further Fed tightening. For crypto traders this combination of energy shock and rate pressure is a classic headwind for Bitcoin and risk assets until clarity emerges.
items.impact: Elevated oil supports higher rates and risk-off flows
